dct_description_sm: The salp species Salpa thompsoni was collected using depth-stratified net sampling across six Southern Ocean regions during nine sampling years between 1989 and 2018. This dataset includes 36 sampling stations that form 13 day-night pairs and 10 single tows (7 daytime, 3 nighttime) from multiple research cruises (SO891, TAN1516, PS112, AG57, TAN0802, LMG09-01, LMG10-01, LMG11-01, LMG17-01) conducted in the Bransfield Strait, Chatham Rise, Elephant Island, Lazarev Sea, Ross Sea, and the Western Antarctic Peninsula. The archived dataset includes 13 day-night sampling pairs; however, the associated manuscript analyzes 12 day-night pairs because the southwestern Lazarev Sea stations (D081–D084) were combined into a single analytical day-night pair following original cruise methodology. Depth-stratified oblique tows were performed using a multi-Rectangular Midwater Trawl system (RMT-1+8) equipped with three 1 m² mouth area nets (330 µm mesh) and three 8 m² mouth area nets (4.5 mm mesh), a Multiple Opening/Closing Net and Environmental Sensing System (MOCNESS-1) with a 1 m² mouth area and nine 200 µm mesh nets, a standard RMT-8 (8 m², 4.5 mm mesh), and Juday nets (0.8 m diameter; effective mouth area ~0.5 m²; 176 µm mesh). Discrete depth intervals ranged from the surface to, in some cases, 1250 m. Each individual was identified by life cycle stage (LCS: blastozooid, oozoid), and when possible, developmental stage and oral-atrial length (OAL, mm), with size class assigned based on maturity. Abundance (ind. m⁻³) was calculated for each depth stratum by dividing the number of individuals by the filtered volume and, where applicable, scaling by depth interval thickness. All sampled depth strata are included, even when S. thompsoni was absent, ensuring complete representation of the vertical sampling effort. Depth strata reflect original sampling intervals from each cruise and may differ from standardized or rounded bins presented in the associated manuscript. This dataset provides depth- and size-resolved estimates of S. thompsoni abundance across life cycle stages, offering key insights into its diel vertical distribution and regional variability.
